runtime.command_template: python tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <libpinmame> --game spectru4 --rom-path <vpinmame-roms> --work-dir <new-isolated-state> --handle-mechanics 0 --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/by35/spectru4-flipper-buttons-and-saucer-7.json --dmd-dir <external-dmd-dir> --output <external-run.json>. Each set_switch holds one public level; the snapshot after each step records player 1's seven-segment score (decoded here as digits) and the active outputs. Public 19 is BY35 continuous bit 2, which the controller profile and lisy35.c name the flipper-enable relay.

named_action_observations.label: credit button: public 6 pressed after two coins on public 11: the ROM starts a game and raises public 19, the flipper-enable relay

checkpoint: the drain saucer kicks: the drain saucer switch (public 8) went to 1 in the step before: the ROM kicks the drain saucer (5) 0.5 s later; transitioned_solenoid_addresses covers the checkpoint step that waits for 5
public 2 to 1 with the ball on the saucer: held 3 s with public 8 still at 1: no solenoid changes, so the ROM does not launch the ball, and public 19 stays raised
public 2 back to 0: held 3 s with public 8 still at 1: no solenoid changes; public 19 stays raised

public 1 to 1 with the ball on the saucer: with public 8 still at 1, the ROM kicks the drain saucer (5) 0.1 s after public 1 rises, the address the table binds to the right flipper key; the previous kick was 9.0 s earlier, the drain saucer's first
public 7 closed in play: the ROM fires the top kicker (1) and the score rises by 10,000 to 10,000; public 19 stays raised
public 2 held at 1 in play: held 3 s: no solenoid changes and public 19 stays raised, so the ROM does not tilt
tilt bob 15 #1: the ROM tilts and drops public 19

raw_runs.name: spectru4-flipper-buttons-and-saucer-7
raw_runs.nvram_initialization: empty; the run created its own isolated PinMAME state directory and sends no keyboard input: after a 15 s boot wait it coins up and starts a game with direct switch writes

source.attribution: Generated locally from pinned PinMAME and the user-authorized ROM corpus; ROM bytes remain external. Public switch writes are host stimuli, never ROM observations. Scores are the harness's seven-segment values for player 1's display, read as digits.
